turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Ms. Harlan, come on in and have a seat. What brings you by?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh, hi. Um, I'm just exhausted. And cold, cold in my bones, even with the thermostat sitting on seventy-two. It's been going on for months.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): Months is a big range. Closer to two, or more like half a year?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Well, actually, I almost said since Christmas, but no, it started before that. Fall. I keep pinning it on work. I'm fifty-two and the office has been a complete circus.
[SEG0005] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I'm Dana, I live in the spare room and help with the house. She's been dragging since September, easy. Gets home, drops the bag, and just sits.
[SEG0006] person_1 (DOCTOR): Appreciate that, Dana. So tired and cold since the fall. What else have you noticed?
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): The weight. I've put weight on, my work pants won't button. And, this is kind of gross, I'm constipated.
[SEG0008] person_1 (DOCTOR): Not gross at all. About how much weight, and what's the bowel pattern?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): Maybe twelve pounds. I didn't exactly weigh myself. I go every three or four days now, hard stools. I used to go every morning.
[SEG0010] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She's been safety-pinning the waistband. That's new for her.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): How's your mood been with all this?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Flat. I don't cry or anything, I just don't care about stuff I liked. I figured that's the job and getting older, you know?
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any hair loss, dry skin, a lump in the neck, or changes with your periods?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Periods stopped a couple years ago, menopause. Skin's dry, yeah. No lump. Hair's thinner, though I color it, so it's tricky to judge.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any chest pain, shortness of breath, or feeling like you might pass out?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): No. None of that.
[SEG0017] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She nods off on the couch after dinner. She never used to.
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): That's true. Oh, and my mom had thyroid trouble. Took a pill for it her whole life. They checked mine once and it was borderline, they said.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Borderline. Any sense of when that was, or what the number was?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): I want to say two years ago? No number stuck. They said borderline and left it. I never started a thyroid medicine.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): I had the old note up. March of twenty twenty-three, the TSH was normal. It wasn't marked borderline. So the chart and what you remember don't line up.
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Huh. I would've sworn they said borderline. Anyway.
[SEG0023] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Her sister sent iron tablets in the spring. Bottle's still sealed in the cabinet. She never took a single one.
[SEG0024] person_1 (DOCTOR): So the iron was never taken.
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): Right, never. The senna I did use, one tablet at night for the constipation. I stopped it in March because it was cramping me up.
[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): Senna, one tablet at night, stopped in March. Anything you take now? Any allergies, to medicines or anything else?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Just a multivitamin, one a day. No allergies that I know of. Oh my gosh, though, the drive over was ridiculous.

[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): We sat on the bridge forty minutes, and a guy in a pickup had the country station so loud the windows buzzed. Then a huge flock of geese went over, hundreds of them, heading south.
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): Made me think of my granddaughter's school play last month. She was a tree, construction-paper leaves and everything. I teared up, the happy kind. Sorry, I wander off.
[SEG0030] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Paper leaves in the cup holder for a week. Weather's been the same way, coat on, coat off.

[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): No harm done, geese aside. You've been tired and cold since the fall, up about twelve pounds, with hard stools every three or four days, a flat mood, dry skin, thinner hair, and naps after supper. Your mother had thyroid disease, the twenty twenty-three TSH was normal on the chart, and you never started thyroid medicine or the iron. Senna stopped in March, you take a multivitamin daily, and you have no allergies.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, that's the picture. I still think it's just the job and my age, though.

[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): Work and age can absolutely wear you down. I'm also thinking this could be an underactive thyroid, and I'd rather check than guess. I want a TSH, a free T4, a blood count, and a basic metabolic panel.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Can they stick me today?
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): If the lab has a slot when we're done, yes, otherwise tomorrow morning. You don't need to fast. Coming before breakfast is fine if it's easy, not a requirement.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): Should I start the senna again, and when am I supposed to come back?

[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): I wouldn't restart the senna. If the constipation is really bothering you before the labs are back, psyllium once a day is fine to try on your own, and I'm not prescribing it. Ease up at work a little this month if you can, and I'll see you in two weeks for the results either way. Call sooner if you get chest pain, if you start vomiting with the constipation, or if you feel markedly worse.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Two weeks, got it. I'll try to leave the geese out of it next time.

spec.situation: Middle-aged person tired and cold for months, weight up, constipated, low mood; pins it on work and age; mother had thyroid disease; one old thyroid test result recalled wrongly ('borderline, they said'). Blood test planned.
features: stopped_or_never_taken: a medicine the patient stopped, was never given or only took once ('I stopped it in March'). Status discontinued, not current; a medicine never taken is not recorded as a medication.
tangent_small_talk: a long tangent or small talk (traffic, cricket, the weather, a grandchild) that holds NO clinical content; nothing from it is extracted.

omissions.text: Patient reported a real discrepancy between her recollection and the chart: she remembered being told her thyroid test was 'borderline' about 2 years ago, but the doctor said the chart shows a normal TSH in March 2023 and that the chart and her memory do not line up.
Patient specifically said she never started any thyroid medicine.
Negative finding not recorded: patient denied hair loss, instead describing hair as thinner.
